s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe upper abdominal pain with associated nausea and vomiting, worsened by oral intake, in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
Cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant on CT with spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain
Pain awakened her early in the morning
Pain rated 9/10
Pain minimally relieved by oxycodone
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Unable to tolerate liquids or a soft diet
History of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass three weeks prior
History of intermittent nausea after gastric bypass
Denies bloating, changes in bowel habits, or urinary symptoms
Medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with pantoprazole, metformin, and semaglutide
History of laparoscopic cholecystectomy and other abdominal surgeries
Generalized abdominal tenderness on examination
Vital signs within normal limits
Laboratory studies showed normal hemoglobin, slightly elevated white-cell count, and normal liver function tests
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant with spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Small Bowel Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake, with CT findings of clustered small-bowel loops

shortlist.label: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass Complication

shortlist.label: Mesenteric Ischemia
